blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Slope is the biggest contributor to landslide susceptibility in the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL), a 2026 study revealed, highlighting the need for stronger preventive measures. Earlier this month, a landslide hit Baras, Rizal, covering 50 meters of Marilaque Highway and temporarily blocking almost four kilometers of the road, Masungi Georeserve said on Facebook, pointing out the landscape’s susceptibility to landslides. Based on the study, “GIS-Based Landslide Susceptibility Assessment of the UMRBPL, Rizal, Philippines,” which used the Analytic Hierarchy Process, slope accounted for 28.04% of the area’s landslide susceptibility, the highest contribution among the factors examined.
